Think "Stalemate" was originally what was actually written in the article and stayed for many years before more recently removed by someone who may not want to admit a stalemate. Nonetheless still benefits from added useful context for readers' convenience as it's accurate to point out such key facts. It's not deniable and gives readers a better and accurate grasp of the results instead of having to dig for it tiresomely.

Generally more accurate to describe the outcome as a "military and political stalemate" rather than "inconclusive". As Stalemate captures both the military deadlock and the political divisions that persisted after the war ended, reflecting neither side achieved their objective. Whereas "inconclusive" is somewhat more vague and doesn't fully convey specific military and political outcomes and the fact that the armistice effectively preserved the status quo.
